datasets.iso_group/process_step:
#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_holc_redlining/download -p /data/mdc_holc_redlining/etl
  chmod 777 /data/mdc_holc_redlining/download
  cd /data/mdc_holc_redlining
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  ogr2ogr -nln mdc_holc_redlining download/mdc_holc_redlining.geojson 'https://services.arcgis.com/jIL9msH9OI208GCb/ArcGIS/rest/services/HOLC_Neighborhood_Redlining/FeatureServer/0/query?where=city=%27Miami%27&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json'
  
  # replace column names Shape__Length and Shape__Area to avoid conflict when
  # providing as service on ArcServer.
  sed -i 's/Shape__Length/shape_length/gI; s/Shape__Area/shape_area/gI' download/mdc_holc_redlining.geojson
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/mdc_holc_redlining.geojson -nlt multipolygon -nln mdc_holc_redlining
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE mdc_holc_redlining
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'mdc_holc_redlining',
    'geom_local', 2236, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE mdc_holc_redlining
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),2236)));
  CREATE INDEX mdc_holc_redlining_geom_local_idx
    ON mdc_holc_redlining
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/mdc_holc_redlining/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/mdc_holc_redlining/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.
  pg_dump <postgres opts> -h gdsc-postgis-node-14tphzahiyxfy9tf -t mdc_holc_redlining > derived/mdc_holc_redlining.sql
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of SQL in derivative directory on postgis
  rm -f derived/mdc_holc_redlining.sql.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/mdc_holc_redlining.sql.tar.gz meta_dcat_mdc_holc_redlining.json -C derived mdc_holc_redlining.sql

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
This dataset is derived from the 2015 Miami-Dade County DEM 10ft layer found at https://gis-mdc.opendata.arcgis.com/documents/MDC::2015-miami-dade-county-dem-10ft/about. The original source data was resampled to a resolution of 30ft per pixel using the gdalwarp utility.
  
  This source from Miami-Dade County a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) as a raster mosaic in ESRI float format 32bit representation on a 10ft grid created from the LiDAR collected for the 2015 ITD LiDAR project.
  
  Bare-earth 10-foot DEM as 32-bit floating point raster format in ArcGIS GRID Raster format in compliance with USGS LIDAR Base Specifications: georeferencing information, delivered without overlap and with no edge artifacts or mismatched, “NODATA” value for void areas, bridges removed from the surface, etc.

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/download -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/etl
  chmod 777 /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/download
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # load mdc_2015_dem_10ft as dependency (see mdc_2015_dem_10ft for details).
  
  # resample raster with:
  gdalwarp -tr 30 30 /data/mdc_2015_dem_10ft/download/dem_10ft/w001000.adf download/mdc_2015_dem_30ft.tif
  
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # load raster into postGIS with:
      raster2pgsql -s 2236 -d -C -I -t 100x100 mdc_2015_dem_30ft.tif -F mdc_2015_dem_30ft > load_raster.sql
  psql <connection options> < load_raster.sql
  rm load_raster.sql
  
  # create color raster
  mkdir -p /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_30ft
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft
  cat > /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_30ft_color_ramp.txt <<_EOF
  nv 0 0 0 0
  22.324 255 255 255 255
  18.136 219 178 142 255
  14.318 208 179 124 255
  10.501 219 200 161 255
  6.684 250 247 187 255
  2.867 210 231 171 255
  -0.30 221 226 183 255
  -0.91 159 207 251 255
  _EOF
  gdaldem color-relief download/mdc_2015_dem_30ft.tif /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_30ft_color_ramp.txt /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_30ft_color.tif -alpha
  # create color raster and render raster tiles 
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived
  mkdir -p /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_30ft
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft
  echo "" | base64 -d > /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_30ft_legend.png
  cp /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_30ft_legend.png /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/
  # render raster tiles 
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/
  gdal2tiles.py -ex --xyz -z 8-16 /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_30ft_color.tif /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_30ft
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_30ft/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.

datasets.collection_group/disclaimer:
Location data for HUD-related properties and facilities are derived from HUD's enterprise geocoding service. While not all addresses are able to be geocoded and mapped to 100% accuracy, we are continuously working to improve address data quality and enhance coverage. Please consider this issue when using any datasets provided by HUD.  When using this data, take note of the field titled “LVL2KX” which indicates the overall accuracy of the geocoded address using the following return codes: 
  ‘R’ - Interpolated rooftop (high degree of accuracy, symbolized as green)  
  ‘4’ - ZIP+4 centroid (high degree of accuracy, symbolized as green) 
  ‘B’ - Block group centroid (medium degree of accuracy, symbolized as yellow)  
  ‘T’ - Census tract centroid (low degree of accuracy, symbolized as red)  
  ‘2’ - ZIP+2 centroid (low degree of accuracy, symbolized as red) 
   ‘Z’ - ZIP5 centroid (low degree of accuracy, symbolized as red) 
  ‘5’ - ZIP5 centroid (same as above, low degree of accuracy, symbolized as red)  
  Null - Could not be geocoded (does not appear on the map)  
  
  For the purposes of displaying the location of an address on a map only use addresses and their associated lat/long coordinates where the LVL2KX field is coded ‘R’ or ‘4’. These codes ensure that the address is displayed on the correct street segment and in the correct census block. The remaining LVL2KX codes provide a cascading indication of the most granular level geography for which an address can be confirmed. For example, if an address cannot be accurately interpolated to a rooftop (‘R’), or ZIP+4 centroid (‘4’), then the address will be mapped to the centroid of the next nearest confirmed geography: block group, tract, and so on. When performing any point-in polygon analysis it is important to note that points mapped to the centroids of larger geographies will be less likely to map accurately to the smaller geographies of the same area. For instance, a point coded as ‘5’ in the correct ZIP Code will be less likely to map to the correct block group or census tract for that address. #########

  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_public_housing/download -p /data/mdc_public_housing/etl
  chmod 777 /data/mdc_public_housing/download
  cd /data/mdc_public_housing
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget -O download/mdc_public_housing.json 'https://services.arcgis.com/VTyQ9soqVukalItT/arcgis/rest/services/Public_Housing_Developments/FeatureServer/0/query?outFields=*&where=COUNTY_LEVEL%3D12086&outSR=4326&f=geojson'
  
  # replace column names Shape__Length and Shape__Area to avoid conflict when
  # providing as service on ArcServer.
  sed -i 's/Shape__Length/shape_length/gI; s/Shape__Area/shape_area/gI' download/mdc_public_housing.json
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/mdc_public_housing.json -nlt point -nln mdc_public_housing
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE mdc_public_housing
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'mdc_public_housing',
    'geom_local', 2236, 'point', 2
  );
  UPDATE mdc_public_housing
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(geom,2236)));
  CREATE INDEX mdc_public_housing_geom_local_idx
    ON mdc_public_housing
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';

  cd /data/mdc_public_housing/
  mkdir -p derived

  cd /data/mdc_public_housing/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.

  rm -f derived/mdc_public_housing.sql.tar.gz

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
This dataset is derived from the 2015 Miami-Dade County DEM 10ft layer found at https://gis-mdc.opendata.arcgis.com/documents/MDC::2015-miami-dade-county-dem-10ft/about. The original source data was resampled to a resolution of 30ft per pixel using the gdalwarp utility.
  
  This source from Miami-Dade County a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) as a raster mosaic in ESRI float format 32bit representation on a 10ft grid created from the LiDAR collected for the 2015 ITD LiDAR project.
  
  Bare-earth 10-foot DEM as 32-bit floating point raster format in ArcGIS GRID Raster format in compliance with USGS LIDAR Base Specifications: georeferencing information, delivered without overlap and with no edge artifacts or mismatched, “NODATA” value for void areas, bridges removed from the surface, etc.
datasets.dublin_core_group/provenance: This dataset is derived from the 2015 Miami-Dade County DEM 10ft layer found at https://gis-mdc.opendata.arcgis.com/documents/MDC::2015-miami-dade-county-dem-10ft/about. The original source data was resampled to a resolution of 100ft per pixel using the gdalwarp utility.

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/download -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/etl
  chmod 777 /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/download
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # load mdc_2015_dem_10ft as dependency (see mdc_2015_dem_10ft for details).
  
  # resample raster with:
  gdalwarp -tr 100 100 /data/mdc_2015_dem_10ft/download/dem_10ft/w001000.adf download/mdc_2015_dem_100ft.tif
  
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # load raster into postGIS with:
      raster2pgsql -s 2236 -d -C -I -t 48x48 mdc_2015_dem_100ft.tif -F mdc_2015_dem_100ft > load_raster.sql
  psql <connection options> < load_raster.sql
  rm load_raster.sql
  
  # create color raster
  mkdir -p /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_100ft
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft
  cat > /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft_color_ramp.txt <<_EOF
  nv 0 0 0 0
  22.324 255 255 255 255
  18.136 219 178 142 255
  14.318 208 179 124 255
  10.501 219 200 161 255
  6.684 250 247 187 255
  2.867 210 231 171 255
  -0.30 221 226 183 255
  -0.91 159 207 251 255
  _EOF
  gdaldem color-relief download/mdc_2015_dem_100ft.tif /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft_color_ramp.txt /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft_color.tif -alpha
  # create color raster and render raster tiles 
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived
  mkdir -p /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_100ft
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft
  echo "" | base64 -d > /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft_legend.png
  cp /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft_legend.png /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/
  # render raster tiles 
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/
  gdal2tiles.py -ex --xyz -z 8-14 /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft_color.tif /tiles/raster/mdc_2015_dem_100ft
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/mdc_2015_dem_100ft/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.
  pg_dump <postgres opts> -h gdsc-postgis-node-yeum0jp5kyd7z8et -t mdc_2015_dem_100ft > derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft.sql
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of SQL in derivative directory on postgis
  rm -f derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft.sql.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/mdc_2015_dem_100ft.sql.tar.gz meta_dcat_mdc_2015_dem_100ft.json -C derived mdc_2015_dem_100ft.sql

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
This feature class has been created to illustrate the water bodies within the Urban Development Boundary (UDB) and outside the UDB, approximately 938 square miles.
  
  A collection of vector polygon features for water bodies within the Urban Development Boundary (UDB) and outside the UDB, approximately 938 square miles. The planimetric layer for Miami-Dade County was previously digitized in 2001 by Woolpert, in 2012 by GPI Geospatial (GPI), and in 2020 by GPI. GPIs 2022 update utilized a Geodatabase provided by ITD for Miami-Dade County containing two layers to be updated: Water and Edge of Pavement. GPI used the recent set of county orthoimages, produced by Woolpert in 2022, to perform the update of the various feature classes. The feature classes were clipped into smaller blocks. Compilers made adjustments or recollected any missing features. The corresponding attributes were assigned to each separate shapefile as adjustments and new collection occurred. The shapefiles were then merged back together into a full file. Topological checks were performed to make sure the linework did not cross unexpectedly, ends dangled, or strange gaps exist in the collected features. Depending on the layer, different checks were done using the existing data layer to evaluate the completeness of the overall collection. The final layers were quality checked for formatting and file corruption before being sent to the client for review. Personnel that collected this data are either photogrammetrists trained in stereo collection or editors trained in ortho-photography based collection. Items included in the feature class WATER BODIES (Polygons) are: Water bodies and water-under-the-bridge features Definition of particular fields in the Water feature class: Water = {0,1} where 0 = Feature does not represent water; 1 = Water feature. Type = {'', 'B'} where B = Water under the bridge. Where '' marks water locations without bridges. Possible combinations of these fields are: 0,''; 1,'';1, 'B'.

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/download -p /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/etl
  chmod 777 /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/download
  cd /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget -O download/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.zip 'https://sedac.ciesin.columbia.edu/downloads/data/sdei/sdei-annual-pm2-5-concentrations-countries-urban-areas-v1-1998-2016/sdei-annual-pm2-5-concentrations-countries-urban-areas-v1-1998-2016-urban-areas-shp.zip'
  
  # unzip to download directory if update flag is set
  if do_update == 1 then
  unzip -d download download/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.zip && rm download/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.zip
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/sdei-annual-pm2-5-concentrations-countries-urban-areas-v1-1998-2016-urban-areas.shp -nlt multipolygon -nln global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016',
    'geom_local', 3857, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),3857)));
  CREATE INDEX global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016_geom_local_idx
    ON global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Create shapefile of table in derivate directory on osgeo 
  ogr2ogr -f "ESRI Shapefile" -overwrite derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp PG:"<postgres connection>" global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of shp in derivative directory on osgeo
  rm -f derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp.tar.gz meta_dcat_global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.json -C derived global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.prj global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shx global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.dbf
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.
  pg_dump <postgres opts> -h gaia-db -t global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016 > derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of SQL in derivative directory on postgis
  rm -f derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql.tar.gz meta_dcat_global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.json -C derived global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql

datasets.dublin_core_group/description: The Annual PM2.5 Concentrations for Countries and Urban Areas, 1998-2016, consists of mean concentrations of particulate matter (PM2.5) for countries and urban areas. The PM2.5 data are from the Global Annual PM2.5 Grids from MODIS, MISR and SeaWiFS Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) with GWR, 1998-2016. The urban areas are from the Global Rural-Urban Mapping Project, Version 1 (GRUMPv1): Urban Extent Polygons, Revision 02, and its time series runs from 1998 to 2016. The country averages are population-weighted such that concentrations in populated areas count more toward the country average than concentrations in less populated areas, and its time series runs from 2008 to 2015

datasets.iso_group/process_step:
#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/download -p /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/etl
  chmod 777 /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/download
  cd /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget -O download/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.zip 'https://sedac.ciesin.columbia.edu/downloads/data/sdei/sdei-annual-pm2-5-concentrations-countries-urban-areas-v1-1998-2016/sdei-annual-pm2-5-concentrations-countries-urban-areas-v1-1998-2016-urban-areas-shp.zip'
  
  # unzip to download directory if update flag is set
  if do_update == 1 then
  unzip -d download download/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.zip && rm download/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.zip
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/sdei-annual-pm2-5-concentrations-countries-urban-areas-v1-1998-2016-urban-areas.shp -nlt multipolygon -nln global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016',
    'geom_local', 3857, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),3857)));
  CREATE INDEX global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016_geom_local_idx
    ON global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Create shapefile of table in derivate directory on osgeo 
  ogr2ogr -f "ESRI Shapefile" -overwrite derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp PG:"<postgres connection>" global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of shp in derivative directory on osgeo
  rm -f derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp.tar.gz meta_dcat_global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.json -C derived global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shp global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.prj global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.shx global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.dbf
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.
  pg_dump <postgres opts> -h gaia-db -t global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016 > derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of SQL in derivative directory on postgis
  rm -f derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql.tar.gz meta_dcat_global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.json -C derived global_pm25_concentration_1998_2016.sql

Social vulnerability refers to the potential negative effects on communities caused by external stresses on human health. Such stresses include natural or human-caused disasters, or disease outbreaks. Reducing social vulnerability can decrease both human suffering and economic loss.
  
  The CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (CDC/ATSDR SVI) uses 16 U.S. census variables to help local officials identify communities that may need support before, during, or after disasters.

Social vulnerability refers to the potential negative effects on communities caused by external stresses on human health. Such stresses include natural or human-caused disasters, or disease outbreaks. Reducing social vulnerability can decrease both human suffering and economic loss.
  
  The CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (CDC/ATSDR SVI) uses 16 U.S. census variables to help local officials identify communities that may need support before, during, or after disasters.

#########

  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/mdc_2022_svi_tract/download -p /data/mdc_2022_svi_tract/etl
  chmod 777 /data/mdc_2022_svi_tract/download
  cd /data/mdc_2022_svi_tract
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # load fl_2022_svi_tract as dependency (see fl_2022_svi_tract for details).
  
  # Create copy of geom dependency
  pg_dump -d $POSTGRES_DB -U $POSTGRES_USER -p $POSTGRES_PORT -h gdsc-postgis-node-3vuojj3i3utqwxih -t fl_2022_svi_tract | sed 's/fl_2022_svi_tract/mdc_2022_svi_tract/g' | psql -d $POSTGRES_DB -U $POSTGRES_USER -p $POSTGRES_PORT -h gdsc-postgis-node-sxztgqd6071bq4ie 
  
  # drop geom_local and subset as per custom parameters
  psql -d $POSTGRES_DB -U $POSTGRES_USER -p $POSTGRES_PORT -h gdsc-postgis-node-sxztgqd6071bq4ie -c "
  ALTER TABLE mdc_2022_svi_tract DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS geom_local;
  DELETE FROM mdc_2022_svi_tract
    WHERE NOT (stcnty = '12086');
  COMMIT;"
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'mdc_2022_svi_tract',
    'geom_local', 2236, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE mdc_2022_svi_tract
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),2236)));
  CREATE INDEX mdc_2022_svi_tract_geom_local_idx
    ON mdc_2022_svi_tract
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'mdc_2022_svi_tract',
    'geom_local', 2236, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE mdc_2022_svi_tract
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),2236)));
  CREATE INDEX mdc_2022_svi_tract_geom_local_idx
    ON mdc_2022_svi_tract
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
VNP46A4 - VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Yearly L3 Global 15 arc second Linear Lat Lon Grid
  
  The Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (SNPP) Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) supports a Day-Night Band (DNB) sensor that provides global daily measurements of nocturnal visible and near-infrared (NIR) light that are suitable for Earth system science and applications. The VIIRS DNB's ultra-sensitivity in lowlight conditions enable us to generate a new set of science-quality nighttime products that manifest substantial improvements in sensor resolution and calibration when compared to the previous era of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program/Operational Linescan System's (DMSP/OLS) nighttime lights image products. Such improvements allow the VIIRS DNB products to better monitor both the magnitude and signature of nighttime phenomena, and anthropogenic sources of light emissions.
  
  VNP46A4 is the short-name for the fourth nighttime lights (NTL) product in the Black Marble suite, which provides yearly composites generated from daily atmospherically- and lunar-BRDF-corrected NTL radiance to remove the influence of extraneous artifacts and biases. Known by its long-name, VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Yearly L3 Global 15 arc-second Linear Lat Lon Grid, this product contains 28 layers. They provide information on the NTL composite, the number of observations, quality, and standard deviation for multi-view zenith angle categories (near-nadir, off-nadir, and all angles), their snow-covered and snow-free statuses besides land-water mask, latitude and longitude coordinate information. They also include detailed information and description of the quality flags. This SNPP VIIRS collection-1 product record, identified by its version-ID 001 in its file name, starts from January 1st 2012.

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/hh_departamentos_minam/download -p /data/hh_departamentos_minam/etl
  chmod 777 /data/hh_departamentos_minam/download
  cd /data/hh_departamentos_minam
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  ogr2ogr -nln hh_departamentos_minam download/hh_departamentos_minam.json 'https://geoservidorperu.minam.gob.pe/arcgis/rest/services/ServicioBase/MapServer/14/query?where=1%3D1&geometry=%22xmin%22%3A-77.33%2C%22ymin%22%3A-10.7%2C%22xmax%22%3A-76.55%2C%22ymax%22%3A-9.8&geometryType=esriGeometryEnvelope&inSR=4326&spatialRel=esriSpatialRelIntersects&outFields=*&where=1%3D1&outSR=4326&f=geojson'
  
  # replace column names Shape__Length and Shape__Area to avoid conflict when
  # providing as service on ArcServer.
  sed -i 's/Shape__Length/shape_length/gI; s/Shape__Area/shape_area/gI' download/hh_departamentos_minam.json
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/hh_departamentos_minam.json -nlt multipolygon -nln hh_departamentos_minam
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE hh_departamentos_minam
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'hh_departamentos_minam',
    'geom_local', 5387, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE hh_departamentos_minam
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),5387)));
  CREATE INDEX hh_departamentos_minam_geom_local_idx
    ON hh_departamentos_minam

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
El primer Inventario Nacional de Bofedales (INB) del Perú tiene como finalidad delimitar y cuantificar el ecosistema de bofedales, con el objetivo de proporcionar información a escala nacional detallada sobre la ubicación y extensión de estos ecosistemas. Esta información busca apoyar la toma de decisiones relacionadas con su gestión sostenible.
  
  La extensión de los bofedales en el Perú se estima en 910 398.2 hectáreas (ha), lo que representa el 0.71% del territorio nacional. Los bofedales están distribuidos en 19 departamentos, siendo Puno, Arequipa y Ayacucho los que concentran más del 50% de la superficie total con aproximadamente de 493 235.2 ha; mientras que los departamentos de Ica, Amazonas y Piura tienen una menor superficie.
  
  El INB se elaboró con un nivel de detalle que permitió cartografiar mediante el uso de técnicas de teledetección unidades mínimas de 0.09 ha, conocido como la Unidad Mínima Cartografiable (UMC). Estas técnicas incluyen el análisis de imágenes satelitales de la constelación Sentinel-1 y Sentinel-2 (correspondientes a la temporada húmeda) y productos DEM - ALOS PALSAR. El análisis se realizó utilizando un clasificador basado en árboles de decisión que integró cinco máscaras como indicadores de presencia de bofedales: altitud (DEM), índice de posición topográfica (TPI), pendiente, índice de humedad (NDII), mixtura espectral (LSU) e intensidad. 
  
  Es importante destacar que para cada máscara se utilizó umbrales específicos definidos según las macrozonas altoandinas (páramo, norte, centro y sur).
  
  Correo electrónico de contacto.
  hmallqui@inaigem.gob.pe, fmedina@inaigem.gob.pe

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
VNP46A4 - VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Yearly L3 Global 15 arc second Linear Lat Lon Grid
  
  The Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership (SNPP) Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) supports a Day-Night Band (DNB) sensor that provides global daily measurements of nocturnal visible and near-infrared (NIR) light that are suitable for Earth system science and applications. The VIIRS DNB's ultra-sensitivity in lowlight conditions enable us to generate a new set of science-quality nighttime products that manifest substantial improvements in sensor resolution and calibration when compared to the previous era of Defense Meteorological Satellite Program/Operational Linescan System's (DMSP/OLS) nighttime lights image products. Such improvements allow the VIIRS DNB products to better monitor both the magnitude and signature of nighttime phenomena, and anthropogenic sources of light emissions.
  
  VNP46A4 is the short-name for the fourth nighttime lights (NTL) product in the Black Marble suite, which provides yearly composites generated from daily atmospherically- and lunar-BRDF-corrected NTL radiance to remove the influence of extraneous artifacts and biases. Known by its long-name, VIIRS/NPP Lunar BRDF-Adjusted Nighttime Lights Yearly L3 Global 15 arc-second Linear Lat Lon Grid, this product contains 28 layers. They provide information on the NTL composite, the number of observations, quality, and standard deviation for multi-view zenith angle categories (near-nadir, off-nadir, and all angles), their snow-covered and snow-free statuses besides land-water mask, latitude and longitude coordinate information. They also include detailed information and description of the quality flags. This SNPP VIIRS collection-1 product record, identified by its version-ID 001 in its file name, starts from January 1st 2012.

datasets.dublin_core_group/description:
Social vulnerability refers to the potential negative effects on communities caused by external stresses on human health. Such stresses include natural or human-caused disasters, or disease outbreaks. Reducing social vulnerability can decrease both human suffering and economic loss.
  
  The CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (CDC/ATSDR SVI) uses 16 U.S. census variables to help local officials identify communities that may need support before, during, or after disasters.

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/download -p /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/etl
  chmod 777 /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/download
  cd /data/ma_2020_svi_tract
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget -O download/ma_2020_svi_tract.zip 'https://svi.cdc.gov/Documents/Data/2020/db/states/Massachusetts.zip'
  
  # unzip to download directory if update flag is set
  if do_update == 1 then
  unzip -d download download/ma_2020_svi_tract.zip && rm download/ma_2020_svi_tract.zip
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/SVI2020_MASSACHUSETTS_tract.gdb -nlt multipolygon -nln ma_2020_svi_tract
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE ma_2020_svi_tract
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'ma_2020_svi_tract',
    'geom_local', 26986, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE ma_2020_svi_tract
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),26986)));
  CREATE INDEX ma_2020_svi_tract_geom_local_idx
    ON ma_2020_svi_tract
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.
  pg_dump <postgres opts> -h gaia-db -t ma_2020_svi_tract > derived/ma_2020_svi_tract.sql
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of SQL in derivative directory on postgis
  rm -f derived/ma_2020_svi_tract.sql.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/ma_2020_svi_tract.sql.tar.gz meta_dcat_ma_2020_svi_tract.json -C derived ma_2020_svi_tract.sql

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/download -p /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/etl
  chmod 777 /data/ma_2020_svi_tract/download
  cd /data/ma_2020_svi_tract
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget -O download/ma_2020_svi_tract.zip 'https://svi.cdc.gov/Documents/Data/2020/db/states/Massachusetts.zip'
  
  # unzip to download directory if update flag is set
  if do_update == 1 then
  unzip -d download download/ma_2020_svi_tract.zip && rm download/ma_2020_svi_tract.zip
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/SVI2020_MASSACHUSETTS_tract.gdb -nlt multipolygon -nln ma_2020_svi_tract
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE ma_2020_svi_tract
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'ma_2020_svi_tract',
    'geom_local', 26986, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE ma_2020_svi_tract
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),26986)));

    ON ma_2020_svi_tract
    USING GIST (geom_local);

  mkdir -p derived

Social vulnerability refers to the potential negative effects on communities caused by external stresses on human health. Such stresses include natural or human-caused disasters, or disease outbreaks. Reducing social vulnerability can decrease both human suffering and economic loss.

datasets.iso_group/process_step:
#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/ma_2022_svi_tract/download -p /data/ma_2022_svi_tract/etl
  chmod 777 /data/ma_2022_svi_tract/download
  cd /data/ma_2022_svi_tract
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  wget -O download/ma_2022_svi_tract.zip 'https://svi.cdc.gov/Documents/Data/2022/db/states/Massachusetts.zip'
  
  # unzip to download directory if update flag is set
  if do_update == 1 then
  unzip -d download download/ma_2022_svi_tract.zip && rm download/ma_2022_svi_tract.zip
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/SVI2022_MASSACHUSETTS_tract.gdb -nlt multipolygon -nln ma_2022_svi_tract
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE ma_2022_svi_tract
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'ma_2022_svi_tract',
    'geom_local', 26986, 'multipolygon', 2
  );
  UPDATE ma_2022_svi_tract
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(ST_Multi(geom),26986)));
  CREATE INDEX ma_2022_svi_tract_geom_local_idx
    ON ma_2022_svi_tract
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/ma_2022_svi_tract/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/ma_2022_svi_tract/
  
  # Create pg_dump of table SQL in derivate directory on postgis.
  pg_dump <postgres opts> -h gaia-db -t ma_2022_svi_tract > derived/ma_2022_svi_tract.sql
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of SQL in derivative directory on postgis
  rm -f derived/ma_2022_svi_tract.sql.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/ma_2022_svi_tract.sql.tar.gz meta_dcat_ma_2022_svi_tract.json -C derived ma_2022_svi_tract.sql

The State Parks are derived as a subset from The Florida Natural Areas Inventory. The Florida Natural Areas Inventory is the primary source for information on Florida's conservation lands. FNAI's database includes boundaries and statistics for more than 2,900 federal, state, local, and private managed areas, all provided directly by the managing agencies. National parks, state forests, wildlife management areas, local and private preserves are examples of the managed areas included. The shapefile is called FLMA for Florida Managed Areas; updated versions are published quarterly.
  
  FLORIDA CONSERVATION LANDS (layer name FLMA): This is a polygon data layer for public (and some private) lands that the Florida Natural Areas Inventory (FNAI) has identified as having natural resource value and that are being managed at least partially for conservation purposes. The term "Managed Area" refers to a managed conservation land.

#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm/download -p /data/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm/etl
  chmod 777 /data/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm/download
  cd /data/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # download if update flag is set:
  if do_update == 1 then
  curl -o download/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.osm 'https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter?data=%28nwr%5B%22place%22~%22city|town|village|hamlet%22%5D%28-10.7,-77.33,-9.8,-76.55%29;%29;%28._;%3E;%29;out;'
  
  # load into postGIS with:
    ogr2ogr -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -f PostgreSQL PG:"<postgres connection>" download/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.osm
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # Select proper geometry into the named table
  psql -d $POSTGRES_DB -U $POSTGRES_USER -p $POSTGRES_PORT -h gdsc-postgis-node-o146127l8nyt4ajh -c "
  SELECT * INTO hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm FROM points;
  DROP TABLE IF EXISTS lines;
  DROP TABLE IF EXISTS multilinestrings;
  DROP TABLE IF EXISTS multipolygons;
  DROP TABLE IF EXISTS other_relations;
  DROP TABLE IF EXISTS points;"
  
  # remove duplicate points and make geometries valid:
  UPDATE hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
    SET geom=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(geom));
  
  # add local geometry column and reproject existing geometries into local EPSG:
  SELECT AddGeometryColumn (
    'hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm',
    'geom_local', 5387, 'point', 2
  );
  UPDATE hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
    SET geom_local=ST_MakeValid(ST_RemoveRepeatedPoints(ST_Transform(geom,5387)));
  CREATE INDEX hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm_geom_local_idx
    ON hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
    USING GIST (geom_local);
  NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Create shapefile of table in derivate directory on osgeo 
  ogr2ogr -f "ESRI Shapefile" -overwrite derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.shp PG:"<postgres connection>" hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of shp in derivative directory on osgeo
  rm -f derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.shp.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.shp.tar.gz meta_dcat_hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.json -C derived hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.shp hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.prj hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.shx hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.dbf
  
  # Create gpkg of table in derivate directory on osgeo 
  rm -f derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.gpkg
  ogr2ogr -f GPKG -overwrite derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.gpkg PG:"<postgres connection>" -select "osm_id,name,highway,other_tags,geom" hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of gpkg in derivative directory on osgeo
  rm -f derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.gpkg.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.gpkg.tar.gz meta_dcat_hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.json -C derived hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.gpkg
  
  # Create geojson of table in derivate directory on osgeo 
  rm -f derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.json
  ogr2ogr -f GeoJSON -overwrite derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.json PG:"<postgres connection>" -select "osm_id,name,highway,other_tags,geom" hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm
  
  # Create downloadable tarfile of geojson in derivative directory on osgeo
  rm -f derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.geojson.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.geojson.tar.gz meta_dcat_hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.json -C derived hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm.json
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/hh_asenamientos_humanos_osm/

datasets.iso_group/process_step:
#########
  # GDSC ETL is performed in two steps: shell script to ETL data into postgres
  # and then additional transformations with SQL in postGIS (if needed).
  ####
  
  #########
  # Step 1 - bash script (pseudo code)
  ####
  
  # create directory structure and move into it
  mkdir -p /data/hh_dem_copernicus/download -p /data/hh_dem_copernicus/etl
  chmod 777 /data/hh_dem_copernicus/download
  cd /data/hh_dem_copernicus
  
  # set update flag based on last update and update frequency
  do_update=0 if date() < last_update + update_frequency else do_update = 1
  
  # clone a git repo and run the code# save netcdf as tif
  cd download
  gdal_translate NETCDF:hh_dem_copernicus.nc:2m_temperature hh_dem_copernicus.tif
  cd ..
  
  
  #########
  # Step 2 - SQL script (pseudo code):
  ####
  
  # load raster into postGIS with:
      raster2pgsql -s 4326 -d -C -I -t auto hh_dem_copernicus.tif -F hh_dem_copernicus > load_raster.sql
  psql <connection options> < load_raster.sql
  rm load_raster.sql
  
  # Move into corrrect directory and create derivative directory in data package on osgeo
  cd /data/hh_dem_copernicus/
  mkdir -p derived
  
  # Create downloadable zip of download/geotiff in derivate directory 
  rm -f derived/hh_dem_copernicus.tif.tar.gz
  tar -czf derived/hh_dem_copernicus.tif.tar.gz meta_dcat_hh_dem_copernicus.json -C download hh_dem_copernicus.tif
  
  # Move into correct directory
  cd /data/hh_dem_copernicus/
